entries.text: The authors claim this is the first deep-learning investigation of ultrasound-to-formant mapping for speech synthesis.
entries.condition: Claimed novelty relative to work known to the authors at publication.

entries.text: The proposed U2F architecture combines spatial and temporal convolutions with channel shuffling as a novel spatio-temporal feature strategy.
entries.condition: Architecture claim; hybrid spatial, temporal, joint-convolution branches followed by channel shuffling.

entries.text: The authors claim to establish the first successful end-to-end mapping from ultrasound tongue images to formant frequencies.
entries.condition: Claim concerns ultrasound tongue-image input and formant-frequency output for SSI research.

entries.text: The authors interpret last-layer saliency maps as evidence that U2F internally represents tongue contours without explicit contour annotations.
entries.condition: Saliency maps correspond to the last CNN layer; the paper reports visual evidence, not contour-label accuracy.

entries.text: The authors say acoustic supervision may replace manual point selection and annotation for tongue-contour tracing.
entries.condition: Stated as potential demonstrated by a non-image-based loss, not as a validated contour-tracing replacement.

entries.text: The joint f1-f2 configuration is reported to perform better than individual-formant prediction despite having fewer parameters.
entries.condition: Comparison is Table 1 joint f1-f2 task versus individual f1 and f2 tasks; parameter counts are not reported.

entries.text: The paper designates the Conv-BiLSTM baseline from Juanpere and Csapó as the state-of-the-art approach.
entries.condition: Baseline reference [11]; the target paper reports its own Table 1 results for this comparator.

entries.text: The authors claim U2F outperforms CNN-RNN and standard 3D-CNN baselines with fewer parameters.
entries.condition: Claim refers to the reported Table 1 regression comparison; exact parameter counts and uncertainty are not given.

entries.text: The authors report 1.88% and 1.44% performance decreases when spatial and temporal encoding are removed, respectively.
entries.condition: U2F ablations on the same dataset; spatial-kernel and temporal-kernel removals, respectively; metric aggregation underlying these changes is not specified.

entries.text: Removing channel shuffling is said to decrease Mean R2 by approximately 0.84%.
entries.condition: U2F ablation without the shuffling block; the aggregation used to calculate the approximate decrease is not specified.

entries.text: The authors claim partial spatial-temporal convolution decoupling is effective in performance and efficient in computation.
entries.condition: Architecture rationale; no runtime, FLOP, or parameter-count measurements are reported in the tables.

entries.text: The authors claim channel shuffling improves cross-group information exchange and spatio-temporal encoding within a computational budget.
entries.condition: Motivated by reference [20]; component contribution is also tested in Table 2.

entries.text: The authors state that U2F may encode robust spatio-temporal information in other related tasks.
entries.condition: Proposed potential is not evaluated on another task in this paper.

entries.text: The authors position the automatic internal contour representation as laying a foundation for an SSI.
entries.condition: This is a stated research contribution; no clinical deployment or post-laryngectomy user evaluation is reported.

entries.text: The paper omits details of the joint parallel-cascaded Klatt synthesis methodology because of space constraints and refers readers to reference [12].
entries.condition: Caveat applies to the formant-to-speech synthesis block, not the formant regression model.

entries.text: The study restricts its acoustic targets to the first two formants, rather than a complete spectral representation.
entries.condition: Formant targets are extracted from recorded speech; the paper calls these the most dominating parameters for speech trajectories.

entries.text: The dataset was collected from one male participant for a personalized SSI study over multiple sessions.
entries.condition: Single male participant; number of sessions and session-wise partition membership are not stated.

entries.text: The number of recording sessions and whether train, development, and test clips are separated by session are not reported.
entries.condition: Single participant recorded over an unspecified number of sessions; random video shuffling is reported but session membership is not.

entries.text: Ultrasound was acquired with an ALOKA SSD-5000 at 30 fps using a convex UST-9118 probe (180 degrees, 9 mm radius, 3.5 MHz).
entries.condition: Mid-sagittal tongue imaging; probe placed beneath the participant's chin.

entries.text: Mono-channel audio was recorded simultaneously in Praat with a Sennheiser MKH 416 P48 microphone and Focusrite Scalet 2i2 preamplifier.
entries.condition: Recorded alongside ultrasound; audio is used to derive the formant targets.

entries.text: Frames at 480×640 pixels were cropped to a tongue-containing 200×330-pixel bounding box.
entries.condition: Ultrasound frame preprocessing before downsampling and grayscale intensity normalization.

entries.text: Cropped ultrasound frames were downsampled to 50×82 pixels.
entries.condition: Input image size after cropping and before sequence assembly.

entries.text: Input ultrasound images were converted to grayscale and pixel intensities normalized to [0, 1].
entries.condition: Image inputs; the paper does not specify normalization of formant-frequency targets.

entries.text: Each input video contains 30 frames, yielding 13,082 videos of one second each.
entries.unit: frames per video; videos; seconds per video
entries.condition: Sequences are extracted from vowel intervals; recordings use 30-fps ultrasound.

entries.text: The single participant produced continuous open-vocal-tract sounds with intervals while seated with the head stabilized against a headset.
entries.condition: Data acquisition involved simultaneous ultrasound and audio; this is not a post-laryngectomy silent-speech cohort.

entries.text: The first hidden layer uses pointwise 3D convolution with a 1×1×1 kernel.
entries.condition: Applied to the input video before the hybrid convolutional layer.

entries.text: The spatial branch uses 2D CNN kernels of size 1×3×3.
entries.condition: Intra-frame spatial branch of the hybrid layer.

entries.text: The temporal branch uses 1D CNN time-kernels of size 3×1×1.
entries.condition: Cross-frame temporal modeling branch of the hybrid layer.

entries.text: The joint spatio-temporal branch uses 3D CNN kernels of size 3×3×3.
entries.condition: Joint spatial-temporal encoding branch of the hybrid layer.

entries.text: Outputs from the three hybrid branches are concatenated and shuffled into three groups.
entries.condition: Channel shuffling is followed by a grouped 1×1×1 convolution.

entries.text: Figure 2 labels the input ultrasound sequence as 1×30×50×82.
entries.condition: Grayscale, 30-frame sequence at 50×82 pixels.

entries.text: The 13,082-video dataset was randomly shuffled into 80% train, 10% development, and 10% test sets.
entries.condition: Randomly partitioned videos from one participant; the paper does not give exact split counts or identify which partition produced Table 1 and Table 2 scores.

entries.text: Formant targets were extracted from Hamming-windowed acoustic blocks of 1,470 samples using LPC and autocorrelation.
entries.condition: Roots of the LPC predictor polynomial were converted to positive frequencies below Nyquist and sorted; f1 and f2 were retained.

entries.text: The regression targets are the first two formant frequencies, f1 and f2, extracted from recorded speech.
entries.condition: Targets come from LPC roots; frequency units and target scaling/normalization are not reported.

entries.text: The model predicts f1 and f2 as sequences of 30 values each for the 30-frame input sequence.
entries.condition: Two task-specific output heads; a joint f1-f2 configuration shares the U2F representation.

entries.text: The final network has four hidden layers, three convolutional layers with 48, 96, and 32 filters, and a 5,760-node fully connected layer.
entries.unit: hidden layers; convolutional layers; filters per convolutional layer; fully connected nodes
entries.condition: U2F model; output heads predict two 30-value formant sequences.

entries.text: Convolutional layers use stride 1, batch normalization, ReLU, and max pooling with stride 2.
entries.condition: Batch normalization follows every convolutional layer and precedes the nonlinearity.

entries.text: Training used batch size 10 on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti GPU.
entries.condition: PyTorch implementation; regression model for the 13,082-video dataset.

entries.text: MAE loss was optimized with Adam at learning rate 0.001 for 100 epochs.
entries.condition: Training objective is mean absolute error on formant sequences.

entries.text: All network parameters were randomly initialized.
entries.condition: The random seed and initialization distribution are not specified.

entries.text: Architectural and hyperparameter choices were made through an exhaustive grid search.
entries.condition: The paper does not state which split or data were used for model selection.

entries.text: Predicted formants are passed as parameters to Klatt synthesis software to generate continuous speech sounds.
entries.condition: Formant-based direct synthesis, not a text or phoneme decoder; synthesis methodology is not fully specified in this paper.

entries.text: No lexical decoder, vocabulary, language model, or other use-time linguistic aid is described; the system maps ultrasound to formants and synthesizes speech.
entries.condition: Continuous formant-based synthesis task; no text-recognition decoding condition is reported.

entries.text: The authors describe the target and predicted acoustic signal as visually almost indistinguishable on one randomly chosen sample.
entries.condition: Qualitative Fig. 3 example only; it is not a corpus-level speech-quality evaluation.

entries.text: Figure 3 shows target and predicted formant trajectories alongside original and synthesized speech signals.
entries.condition: Figure caption; plotted example is a qualitative illustration, not a listening study.

entries.text: No post-laryngectomy participant study, real-time latency, usability evaluation, or deployed SSI trial is reported; the authors frame the system as a foundation for SSI.
entries.condition: Data came from one male participant producing open-vocal-tract sounds with simultaneous audio; clinical generalization and deployment are not evaluated.

entries.text: Although a 10% test split is described, Tables 1 and 2 do not explicitly identify the scored partition or state that their values are test-set results.
entries.condition: Reported scores are regression metrics for the randomly partitioned 13,082-video dataset; exact test-set count and evaluation subset are unstated.

entries.text: No speaker-disjoint or participant-held-out evaluation is reported; all data originate from a single participant and are randomly split as videos.
entries.condition: Single-speaker clip-level evaluation; session overlap across partitions is also unspecified.

entries.text: No random seed, number of training runs, or repeated-split protocol is reported, and no across-run variability is given.
entries.condition: The model uses random initialization and a random data shuffle; table values are presented without run counts or dispersion.

entries.text: The grid-search selection data and whether the development split was used for tuning or model selection are not specified.
entries.condition: A development set is named, but its role in the exhaustive search is not stated.

entries.text: Formant-label scaling or normalization and the frequency units used for the MAE values are not stated.
entries.condition: Pixel normalization is stated for input images, but no corresponding formant-target normalization is described.

entries.text: No chance-level or trivial-regressor reference is defined for the MAE and Mean R2 regression results.
entries.condition: Table comparisons include neural-network baselines and U2F ablations only.

entries.text: The precise aggregation of MAE and R2 across time steps, videos, or output heads is not specified.
entries.condition: The paper says each f1/f2 prediction is a 30-value sequence and names MAE and Mean R2, without defining aggregation axes.

entries.text: No listener test or objective synthesized-speech intelligibility or quality metric is reported; synthesis is illustrated visually for one sample.
entries.condition: Quantitative evaluation focuses on formant regression using MAE and Mean R2.

entries.text: The authors claim fewer parameters for joint U2F and baseline comparisons, but give no exact parameter counts.
entries.condition: Parameter-count basis for the superiority and shared-representation claims cannot be independently compared from the reported tables.

entries.text: The abstract reports a best-model R-squared of 99.96%.
entries.condition: Abstract does not name the task configuration; Table 1 associates 99.96% with U2F joint f1-f2 prediction; evaluation partition is unspecified.

entries.text: The cohort comprised one 42-year-old Hungarian female subject with normal speaking abilities.
entries.condition: subjects/speakers: one; female; Hungarian; age 42

entries.text: She read 438 sentences aloud, so the recorded production was ordinary speech rather than silent articulation.
entries.condition: subjects/speakers: one; production mode: read aloud

entries.text: Ultrasound and audio were synchronized during acquisition of the aloud-read speech corpus; this was not silent articulation.
entries.condition: subjects/speakers: one; production mode: aloud-read speech

entries.text: The 438 utterances were split into 310 training, 41 development, and 87 test utterances.
entries.condition: same single-speaker aloud-read corpus
entries.quote:
The 438 recordings were split
to form a training set, a development set and a test set (310,
41 and 87 utterances, respectively).

entries.text: One subject was recorded across four sessions; the evaluation examines session transfer and provides no speaker-held-out test, so it does not establish generalization to unseen speakers.
entries.condition: Test set: session-specific recordings of the Hungarian tale The North Wind and the Sun; one female speaker across sessions; no speaker split reported.

entries.text: The main cross-session test trained on session 1 and evaluated the unadapted model on test utterances from sessions 2, 3, and 4.
entries.condition: Training: 200 independent sentences from session 1. Test: 9 North Wind and the Sun utterances in each of sessions 2-4. Same speaker; Hungarian fixed-text test; no decoding/LM or seeds reported.

entries.text: Target-session adaptation data were allowed: the model was further trained with 1, 5, 10, 20, or 50 sentences from the current session before testing on that session's nine tale utterances.
entries.condition: Test: 9 North Wind and the Sun utterances from the same target session; same speaker; Hungarian fixed text; no decoding/LM or seeds reported.

entries.text: The objective metric is mean Pearson correlation over the 25 predicted speech-synthesis parameters.

questions.q: Do the reported scores establish speaker-independent performance?
questions.answer: No. All videos came from one male participant and were randomly partitioned as videos; no speaker-held-out test or cross-speaker evaluation is reported.

questions.q: Are Table 1 and Table 2 results explicitly identified as held-out test-set scores?
questions.answer: No. The paper reports an 80/10/10 split but does not say which split generated the table values; seeds, repetitions, and score aggregation are also unspecified.

questions.q: Does the paper validate a clinical silent-speech interface for post-laryngectomy users?
questions.answer: No such validation is reported. The study maps ultrasound to the first two formants and illustrates Klatt-synthesized audio, while its data come from one male participant and its conclusion describes a foundation for SSI.
